modules.name: Inert Pair Effect and Oxidation States

blocks.title: CORE CONCEPTS
blocks.text:
• While moving down the group, the stability of the lower oxidation state (2 less than the group oxidation state) progressively increases, and for element like Tl, Pb, Bi  of the group 13,14 & 15 the stability of the lower oxidation state increases than the group oxidation state. This is called the inert pair effect.

  • Reason: As we move down the group, there is the presence of d & f-orbitals in inner shells, which have poor shielding effect; hence, $Z_{eff}$ increases. As a result, the $ns^2$ electron pair becomes increasingly tightly held to the nucleus and becomes inert /passive towards bonding.
  • Inert Pair Effect is applicable on Group 13, 14 and 15 only.

blocks.title: Points to Remember
blocks.text:
Examples :

1. $PbCl_2$ is more stable than PbCl4.

2. $TlCl$ is more stable than $TlCl_3$.

3. $GaCl_3$ is more stable than $TlCl_3$.

4. $SnCl_4$ is more stable than $PbCl_4$.

5. Thallium (III) iodide does not exist.

6. $PbF_4$, $PbCl_4$ exist but $PbBr_4$ and $PbI_4$ does not exist.

blocks.title: Illustrative Memorizing Facts
blocks.text:
• Thallium (Tl): Common oxidation states +1 and +3; +1 is more stable due to the inert pair effect.
  • Lead (Pb): Common oxidation states +2 and +4; +2 is more stable due to the inert pair effect.
  • Bismuth (Bi): Common oxidation states +3 and +5; +3 is more stable due to the inert pair effect.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.question:
Which compound does not exist ?

(1) $TlCl_3$

(2) $TlI_3$

(3) $BiF_5$

(4) $PbI_4$
blocks.answer:
option no 4

Stable oxidation no. of Pb is +2 due to inert pair effect .

so $PbI_4$ does not exist.

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.question:
In which of the following compounds does the inert pair effect play a significant role?

A) PbCl₂

B) CH₄

C) PCl₅

D) B₂H₆
blocks.answer:
option no. 1 is correct

Solution :

due to inert pair effect Pb shows +2 stable oxidation state.

blocks.title: EXERCISE
blocks.question:
Which of the following statements is correct:

(1) All halogens form $HOXO_3$ type oxy acid

(2) Only chlorine and bromine form oxyacids

(3) All halogens form oxyacids

(4) Only iodine forms oxyacid
blocks.answer:
The correct statement is: (3) All halogens form oxyacids.

Explanation:

All halogens (fluorine, chlorine, bromine, iodine) can form oxyacids, but the stability and number of oxyacids vary among them. Fluorine forms only one (HOF, hypofluorous acid) due to its high electronegativity. Chlorine, bromine, and iodine form several oxyacids, such as hypochlorous acid (HOCl), chlorous acid (HClO₂), chloric acid (HClO₃), and perchloric acid (HClO₄), and their bromine and iodine analogues.
options: (2) Only chlorine and bromine form oxyacids

blocks.title: CORE CONCEPTS
blocks.text:
Hydrolysis :

Hydrolysis is a nucleophilic substitution reaction in which  $H_2O$ (water)acts as the nucleophile.

For hydrolysis, the electrophile should have a vacant orbital as it undergoes  $SN^2$ a mechanism. In general, hydrolysis is a non-redox reaction.

blocks.title: Points to Remember
blocks.text:
Hydrolysis Reaction:

  • $\text{MX} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{MOH} + \text{HX}$
  • Note: X is a halide or another leaving group, assumes complete dissociation.
Stability of Hydrides:

  • $\text{Stability} \propto \frac{1}{\text{Size of Central Atom}}$
  • Note: Smaller central atoms form more stable hydrides.
  • $\text{SiCl}_4 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{SiO}_2 + 4\text{HCl}$
  • Note: Formation of silica and hydrochloric acid.
Note:( $\text{NH}_3$ )Ammonia is a stable hydride of nitrogen.

Bond Strength:

  • $\text{H-F}$ bond is stronger than $\text{H-Cl}$ bond
  • Notes: HF is a weak acid due to strong bond, whereas HCl is stronger.

blocks.title: COMMON MISTAKES
blocks.text:
• Misconception: Assuming all hydrides are ionic.

  • Reality: Many are covalent, especially with non-metals.
  • Misunderstanding Hydrolysis: Confusing it with hydration.
  • Hydrolysis involves chemical change, hydration involves physical water addition.

modules.name: Allotropes and Physical Properties of P-Block Elements

blocks.title: CORE CONCEPTS
blocks.text:
• Allotropes: Different structural forms of the same element, with distinct physical and chemical properties due to variations in bonding and arrangement.

  • Physical Properties: Properties such as melting and boiling points, electrical conductivity, and density are influenced by atomic structure and bonding characteristics.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.question: Identify the electrical conductivity of graphite and diamond and explain the reason for the difference.
blocks.prompt: Identify the electrical conductivity of graphite and diamond and explain the reason for the difference.

blocks.title: COMMON MISTAKES
blocks.text:
• Confusing the electrical conductivity of graphite and diamond; remember graphite is a conductor, diamond is an insulator.
  • Misunderstanding allotropes as different elements rather than different forms of the same element.
